You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions.
Tat Tvam Asi — Thou art That.

"The Self is not born, nor does it die. It has not come into being, does not come into being, and will not come into being. It is unborn, eternal, ever-existing, and primeval. It is not slain when the body is slain."
"Awake, arise, and learn by approaching the exalted ones. The path is sharp as the edge of a razor, difficult to traverse — so say the wise."
"Om iti ekaksharam brahma — Om, this syllable is all this. All that is past, present, and future — all of this is just Om."

"Brahman is reality, knowledge, and infinity. One who knows Brahman as existing in the supreme space within the heart becomes one with Brahman and enjoys all desires simultaneously with the all-knowing Brahman."
"The Self cannot be pierced by weapons or burned by fire; water cannot wet it, nor can the wind dry it."
"Two birds, inseparable companions, perch on the same tree. One eats the fruits, the other looks on without eating."
"That which is the finest essence — this whole world has that as its soul. That is Reality. That is Atman. That art thou, Shvetaketu."
"The wise one who knows the Self as bodiless within the bodies, as unchanging among changing things, as great and omnipresent — that wise one grieves not."
"There are two selves — the separate ego and the indivisible Atman. When one rises above I and me and mine, the Atman is revealed as one's real Self."
"The knower of Brahman becomes Brahman."
"This Atman cannot be attained by the study of the Vedas, nor by intelligence, nor by much hearing. It is attained by the one whom the Self chooses. To such a one, the Self reveals its own nature."
"The infinite is bliss. There is no bliss in anything finite. Only the infinite is bliss."
"Out of millions of human beings, scarcely one strives for perfection, and of those who strive and succeed, scarcely one knows Me in truth."
"The mind is everything. What you think, you become."
"I am the Atman that dwells in the heart of every mortal creature; I am the beginning, the life-span, and the end of all."
"Let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them."

"Higher than the senses are the objects of sense. Higher than the objects of sense is the mind. Higher than the mind is the intellect. Higher than the intellect is the great Atman. Higher than the great Atman is the unmanifest. Higher than the unmanifest is the Purusha. Higher than the Purusha there is nothing at all. That is the end of the journey, that is the final goal."
"The whole universe is Brahman. In tranquility, let one worship It as that from which one came forth, as that into which one will be dissolved, as that in which one breathes."

"It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, the breath of breath, and the eye of the eye. Having detached the Self from the senses, the wise, on departing from this world, become immortal."

"The Self is subtler than the subtle, greater than the great. It is hidden in the heart of every creature. One who is free from desire sees the glory of the Self through the grace of the Creator and becomes free from sorrow."
"I am the taste of water, the light of the sun and the moon, the syllable Om in the Vedas, the sound in ether, and the ability in man."
"Brahman is consciousness. Brahman is bliss. He who knows this becomes Brahman itself."
"The Self alone is the whole world. The Self is the origin, the dissolution, and the final goal. Only the Self exists — recognize this and be free."
"He who sees all beings in the Self and the Self in all beings, he never turns away from it."
"The light that shines above the heavens and above this world, the light that shines in the highest world, beyond which there are no others — that is the light that shines in the hearts of men."
"Meditate on the Self as Om. May you be successful in crossing over to the farther shore, beyond all darkness."

"In the beginning, all this was Brahman alone. It was infinite. It was infinite to the east, infinite to the south, infinite to the west, infinite to the north, and above and below — infinite in every direction. For him, there is no east or west, no above or below, no north or south. The infinite is the Self."
"He moves, and he moves not. He is far, and he is near. He is within all, and he is outside all."
"The Self is the friend of those who have conquered themselves. For those who have not conquered themselves, the Self acts like an enemy."

"Smaller than the smallest, greater than the greatest, this Self forever dwells within the hearts of all. A person freed from desire, with mind and senses purified, beholds the glory of the Self and is without sorrow."
"You are what your deep, driving desire is. As your desire is, so is your will. As your will is, so is your deed. As your deed is, so is your destiny."

"The Self is indeed Brahman — this Self which is made of consciousness, made of mind, made of breath, made of seeing, made of hearing, made of earth, made of water, made of wind, made of space, made of light and of what is not light, made of desire and of what is not desire, made of anger and of what is not anger, made of what is righteous and of what is unrighteous, made of everything."
"Awake, arise, and learn by approaching the excellent. The knowers say the path is as difficult to walk as a razor's edge."
"Om is the bow, the Self is the arrow, and Brahman is the target. With a tranquil heart, take aim. Lose thyself in Brahman, as the arrow is lost in the target."
"Brahman is reality, knowledge, and infinity."
"The Self cannot be pierced by weapons or burned by fire; water cannot wet it, nor can the wind dry it."
"Two birds, inseparable companions, perch on the same tree. One eats the fruits of the tree; the other looks on without eating."
"That which is the finest essence — this whole world has that as its soul. That is Reality. That is Atman. That art thou."

"When all the desires that surge in the heart are renounced, the mortal becomes immortal. When all the knots that strangle the heart are loosened, the mortal becomes immortal. This sums up the teaching of the scriptures."

"The Self is the light that shines in the heart of man, smaller than the smallest atom, greater than the greatest spaces. When the senses are stilled, when the mind is at rest, that highest state is known."
"Om ity etat aksharam idam sarvam" — "Om — this syllable is all this. All that is past, present, and future is indeed Om. And whatever transcends the three divisions of time, that too is Om."
"The knower of Brahman becomes Brahman."
"Never the spirit was born; the spirit shall cease to be never. Never was time it was not; End and Beginning are dreams."
"Out of abundance He took abundance and still abundance remained."
"The Self is not born, nor does it die. It has not come from somewhere, nor has it become anyone. Unborn, eternal, ever-existing, and primordial, it is not slain when the body is slain."
"There are two selves, the separate ego and the indivisible Atman. When one rises above I and me and mine, the Atman is revealed as one's real Self."
"Arise! Awake! Having reached the great teachers, understand. Sharp as a razor's edge, hard to traverse, difficult of going is that path — so the wise declare."
